title: Cut-Out Letter Note
statement:
You want to glue together the text note from letters cut out of the text magazine. Every letter in the magazine can be cut out and used only once. Letter order and position in the magazine do not matter.

Return true if the note can be built, otherwise false. Both strings contain only lowercase letters.

examples.why: "retreat" has 2 e's, 1 r and 2 t's; the note needs 1 t, 1 r and 2 e's.
All letters of "tree" appear in "trek", but there is only one e. Checking that each letter exists is not enough; the counts matter.
The magazine has no a at all.

hints: Order does not matter here, only how many of each letter you have. What structure counts things?
Count the letters of the magazine. Then go through the note and spend one count for each letter you use.
With a 26-slot array: increment for each magazine letter, decrement for each note letter, and fail as soon as any slot goes below zero.

explain.intuition:
Because order does not matter, a text is just a bag of letters. The question is whether the magazine's bag contains the note's bag: for every letter, the magazine must have at least as many copies as the note uses.

Count the magazine once into 26 slots, then walk the note and take one from the matching slot for each letter. The moment a slot would go negative, you have run out of that letter. Searching and deleting letters inside the magazine string instead works too, but each search is O(m), which turns the whole thing into O(n·m).
steps: If note is longer than magazine, return false right away.
Count every letter of magazine into an array of 26 zeros.
For each letter of note, decrement its count. If the count is now below 0, return false.
pitfalls: Checking only that each letter appears in the magazine. "tree" needs two e's, and "trek" has one.
Comparing sets of distinct letters for the same reason.
Searching the magazine string for every letter and cutting it out. Correct, but quadratic on long inputs.

solutions.title: Cut letters out of a copy
solutions.idea: Keep the magazine as a list. For each note letter, find it and remove it; if it is missing, fail.

solutions.title: Count letters
solutions.idea: Count the magazine's letters into 26 slots, then spend them on the note's letters.

followups: The letters can be any Unicode characters. What changes?
Many notes are checked against the same magazine. What do you precompute?
